Name: Mei
Description: Kōsen's former chef de cuisine cooking French food through a Japanese lens, with house dry-aged duck and an 8-seat, 10-course chef's counter.
Rationale: Hits nearly every marker in your dining profile: chef-driven, French + Japanese (both on your list), an intimate refined room, and a Michelin-starred pedigree (owners Johnny & Jimmy Tung run Kōsen). The chef's counter is the anniversary-level option on this list.
Notes: Book: OpenTable. Yelp ~24 reviews · OpenTable 4.6 food/service/ambience

Name: Lumbre
Description: The Michelin-starred Rocca team's wood-fire Spanish kitchen: Ibérico pork collar off the hearth, pan con tomate on bread baked daily, and a 14-gin G&T bar.
Rationale: Spanish is on your list, and Tastes Pretty Good (Rocca, Bar Terroir, Streetlight) has the best track record in the region. Chef-owner Nick Orr ran Rocca's kitchen for years. Quality is Michelin-level at friendlier prices, in a polished but not scene-y room.
Notes: Book: Website / OpenTable. Yelp 4.9 (early) · OpenTable service 4.8

Name: Rio Izakaya
Description: A serious yakitori counter grilling 14 chicken cuts over Japanese white charcoal, plus dry-aged nigiri and a 13-course yakitori omakase for $87.
Rationale: Japanese is on your list, and this is the purist end of it: named technique (binchōtan), dry-aged fish, daily-milled rice. It's the only true yakitori omakase in the area, and the most consistently glowing user reviews of any opening this year.

Name: Marcel St. Pete
Address: 1225 Dr. M.L.K. Jr. St N, St. Petersburg, FL 33701
Description: Burgundy-born chef Jeremy Duclut's second Marcel (after Sarasota's acclaimed Marcel DW): rabbit pot pie à la moutarde, sweetbread gratin and scallops in a vaulted room with a long bistro patio.
Rationale: French bistro is on your list, and the chef already has a track record in Sarasota. It's an intimate, quiet, owner-run room, which fits your romantic-intimate preference. Rated provisionally; I'd revisit the rating after another month of reviews.
Notes: Book: OpenTable. Too new for a Yelp page; OpenTable & Tripadvisor listings live

Name: Tommy's Chophouse
Description: Charleston's Burwell's founder brings an independent Wagyu steakhouse to the 1910s Kress building, with a former bank vault as its private dining room.
Rationale: You wanted a steakhouse but no chains, and this is the only independent, chef-led one to open this year. The historic architecture and the vault room make it feel like an occasion. It ranks lowest of the five because the review base is thin and the energy may run loud.
